key_insight: A large randomized controlled trial at ICLR 2025 shows that LLM-generated feedback applied in the peer-review process makes reviews measurably more informative and increases reviewer–author engagement.
problem_solved: Addresses low-quality, terse, or unconstructive peer reviews and the scalability challenge of providing actionable, constructive feedback that helps authors improve their submissions and fosters productive reviewer–author dialogue.
method: Large-scale randomized controlled design: reviewers (or review instances) were randomly assigned to receive LLM-generated feedback versus control.
LLM feedback provided as targeted suggestions to improve clarity, critique depth, and actionable recommendations; outcomes measured on review informativeness and reviewer–author engagement.
Quantitative analysis comparing treated vs. control groups for key metrics (informativeness, response rates, author uptake) to assess causal impact.
impact: Demonstrates a practical, scalable intervention to raise peer-review quality and encourage constructive interaction between reviewers and authors—useful for conference organizers, journal editors, and platform builders seeking to improve review processes.
visual_elements: Bar chart comparing review informativeness (treated vs. control) with effect size indicated
Flow diagram of experimental workflow: randomization → LLM feedback injection → review submission → outcome measurement
Before/after example: short original review vs. same review improved with LLM suggestions (callouts highlighting added specifics and actionable items)
Engagement timeline or stacked bars showing increased reviewer–author replies and follow-up interactions in the LLM-assisted arm
paper_title: A large-scale randomized study of large language model feedback in peer review
paper_authors: Nitya Thakkar, Mert Yuksekgonul, Jake Silberg, Animesh Garg, Nanyun Peng
